class.name: FSAnnotation
class.brief_description: A read-only description of a single annotation applied to a [FoundryScript] declaration.
class.description: Describes one resolved use of a passive annotation on a class, method, member variable, signal, or constant, such as [code]@timeout(10.0)[/code], [code]@cases(provider = "crit_rows")[/code], or a built-in [code]@export_range(0, 100)[/code]. Instances are produced by the FoundryScript reflection APIs and are immutable snapshots of the compiled annotation metadata. The argument accessors return copies, so mutating them does not change the script's stored annotation data. Values supplied positionally appear in [member args]; values supplied by name appear in [member kwargs]. Defaults declared on the annotation are validated but are not injected into either collection. Both user-declared custom annotations and Godot's built-in engine annotations (such as [code]@export[/code], [code]@onready[/code], or [code]@rpc[/code]) are surfaced as [FSAnnotation] objects; use [member builtin] to tell them apart. Built-in annotations are positional-only, so their arguments always appear in [member args] and [member kwargs] is empty. Script-configuration annotations applied by the parser ([code]@tool[/code], [code]@icon[/code], [code]@static_unload[/code]) are not reflected.

members.member: The positional argument values supplied at the annotation use site, in source order. Each call returns an independent snapshot. Empty for marker annotations or annotations used with only named arguments.

[code]true[/code] when this describes one of Godot's built-in engine annotations (such as [code]@export[/code] or [code]@rpc[/code]); [code]false[/code] for a user-declared custom annotation. Lets reflection consumers filter built-in annotations apart from custom ones.

The named argument values supplied at the annotation use site, keyed by the declaration's parameter name. Each call returns an independent snapshot. Empty when no named arguments were supplied, and always empty for built-in annotations, which are positional-only.
The annotation's short name, without the leading [code]@[/code] (for example [code]&"timeout"[/code]).

The annotation's canonical declaration identity, including its namespace (for example [code]&"cafecito.test.timeout"[/code]). Equal to [member name] when the annotation is declared in the global namespace.
